Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the onboarding checklist. I've attached our current VAT certificate and Italian company registry extract (both PDFs). A couple questions as we complete Redwood's vendor form:

- For EU sales to Redwood, do you require invoices with VAT applied or should we issue net-of-VAT with the EU reverse-charge statement? Our default for international SaaS customers is to use reverse charge when the buyer is VAT-registered in the EU.
- For the PO, can you confirm whether Redwood will put the PO net amount or gross? That affects how we populate the invoice template.
- Are there any specific fields Redwood mandates on the invoice (PO number, legal entity name, VAT number format)?

I've attached: acme_vat_certificate_2026.pdf, acme_company_registry_it.pdf, and our completed onboarding sheet (acme_onboarding_form.xlsx).

We can accept Net30 payment terms. Please let me know the PO number when it's created and if you need any additional tax residency paperwork.

Best,

Hi Luca — thanks for sending these over and for filling the onboarding sheet. Quick responses inline below, plus a couple of asks for finance/procurement: 

- Reverse charge: We can accept invoices net-of-VAT with the standard EU reverse-charge wording if Redwood is listed on the invoice with our EU VAT number. Please include the reverse-charge statement: "VAT exempt under Article 196 of Council Directive 2006/112/EC (reverse charge)."
- PO presentation: Redwood issues POs as net amounts (we record tax treatment on our side). Please populate the invoice with the net amount and a line that shows VAT = 0 with the reverse-charge reference.
- Required invoice fields: PO number (once we issue), invoice number, invoice date, AcmeCloud legal name and VAT ID, Redwood Inference legal entity (Redwood Inference Ltd. / EU VAT: GB999999999 or local entity per region — procurement will confirm exact VAT ID for your invoices), bank details, and currency (EUR).

Action items for us: @karthik_iyer can you confirm the exact Redwood legal entity name and VAT ID we should put on their invoice for routing in AP? @mina_haddad and @ben_carter — can you review the attached onboarding form and the VAT cert for any red flags? Also, we usually require a signed vendor-tax-evidence checklist for EU suppliers so our tax team can file the reverse-charge documentation. I've uploaded the onboarding form to the shared procurement folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cProcurementDocs

Luca — once we have the vendor checklist and confirmation on the legal entity to reference, we will raise a PO. Expected turnaround is 3–5 business days for the PO creation.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Thanks for looping me in. A few technical notes from tax/finance: 

- VAT ID verification: Luca, thank you for the registry extract. Please confirm the VAT ID in this format: IT12345678901 (no spaces). We'll validate against VIES. If it fails VIES, we will need a VAT registration confirmation from your local chamber of commerce.
- Vendor-tax-evidence: We have a short checklist we require for EU vendors (business purpose, VAT reg copy, PO mapping). I'm attaching the vendor-tax-evidence-checklist.pdf — please complete and sign. This allows AP/tax to apply reverse charge treatment in our books.
- PO and invoice routing: Redwood will create a PO that lists the net amount. Finance may require the invoice to explicitly state "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by recipient" and to include our EU legal entity. If AcmeCloud requests gross invoicing, that will complicate tax reclaim and likely delay payment.

Next steps (internal): @mina_haddad please review the VAT cert against our checklist; @ben_carter please flag any unusual banking references (SEPA IBAN, intermediary bank notes).

Attachment: vendor-tax-evidence-checklist.pdf

-Karthik
Director, Finance (Indirect Tax)
Redwood Inference
